name: 61 Ursae Majoris
description: A naked-eye star 9.6 parsecs away, 94% of the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 101501: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.91 +/- 0.009 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 0.94 +/- 0.01

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 101501: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5270 +/- 32

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 101501: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 104.03 +/- 0.26 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 10 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 94% of the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 0.91 milliarcseconds, which gives 0.94 solar radii and 5,270 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 101501: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
